title: The Boundary Walk
logline: Months after their father's death, siblings and a surveyor walk the old family land together, and every fence post seems to remember something different.
human_question: What does losing a parent make family members want that they didn't want before?

premise.story: Adult siblings, after settling their late parent's estate, walk their inherited land with a surveyor to formalise boundaries that were always understood, never drawn.
premise.place: Family paddy or garden land in a rural district.
premise.experience: Chains and measuring instruments in tall grass, old deeds spread on a car bonnet, siblings pointing to trees and fences they each remember differently.

concept_links.why: The source defines covetousness as wanting something that belongs to another to become one's own [C058-P:L224-L229]. A land survey after a parent's death is exactly where that wanting, ordinary and understandable, becomes visible.
The source treats what a life leaves unresolved as its own kind of unfinished action [C057-P:L87]. An undivided inheritance is one very common form of that.

what_camera_could_observe: Measuring the land with chains or modern instruments
Old deeds and photographs laid out
A disagreement handled with more or less grace
A shared meal or a quiet departure at day's end
what_must_be_real: A family that genuinely wants this filmed and controls what is shown. No sibling is cast as 'the greedy one'; the film does not take a side in any real dispute.

possible_arc.opening: The surveyor's van arriving, old deeds unfolded.
possible_arc.turn: A boundary that two siblings remember differently.
possible_arc.ending_open: The measurements are recorded. Whether the family stays easy with each other is left open.

requirements: A family willing to have a real land settlement filmed, in full agreement among all parties
A licensed surveyor willing to be filmed at work

suggestions.name: A rural district with family paddy or garden holdings
suggestions.why: Both regions have common smallholder family land of the kind this story needs; no specific family identified.

risks: Turning a private family conflict into entertainment
Casting any one relative as the villain
Legal sensitivity around real property disputes
drop_if: The dispute is too raw or contested to film responsibly

connections.note: A companion piece on wanting what belongs to another, here among family rather than strangers.
A different possible response to the same pressure: repair through service rather than dispute over property.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
